<!-- board: a new outfit behind a scouter | the first RISC-V board: RockBase NM-CYD-C5 (BETA) | the aquarium and the wizard draw leaner -->
**Over 9000.** Last time, Legends got an aura. This time Squachy found out what those sunglasses are for. Tap his shades while the aura is lit and a scouter flips down over one lens, hunts about, and starts reading his power level. It climbs. It climbs some more. Then it reads a number no scouter should have to read, and goes off like a firework. He takes it well.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.28.0/docs/over-9000.gif" width="480" alt="Squachy on his main screen wrapped in the aura, then a green scouter over his right lens reading a number that climbs past nine thousand and bursts. Then Squachy as OVER 9000: tall gold spiked hair, an orange gi with one sleeve torn off, static crackling over him, on two backgrounds. Then the aquarium, and a plain scene captioned for the new ESP32-C5 board."></p>

**OVER 9000.** The sixteenth outfit, and the first one you have to be a Legend to reach, or own the lot. Gold hair standing up in tall spikes with one lock fallen over his shades, an orange gi with the left sleeve torn clean off, a blue belt, wristbands and boots. Static crawls over him the whole time, and now and then a bolt goes down his side and hits the floor. With the aura behind it, it's rather a lot. That was the idea. While the aura is lit his idle chatter drops hints about the shades on any background, the way the other hidden outfits hint on theirs.

**Squads can hold seventeen outfits now.** Yzzerd filled the last slot the squad radio had for telling each other what they're wearing, so there's one more bit of it. A board on an older release will see a visiting OVER 9000 as plain Squachy. A wrong hat, not a crash, which is the deal this radio has always made.

**The first RISC-V board.** The RockBase NM-CYD-C5 is the classic 2.8" CYD's glass and touch on an **ESP32-C5**: dual-band Wi-Fi 6, 16 MB of flash, 8 MB of extra memory, and a completely different kind of processor. Huge thanks to quietradio, who did the port, wrote a display driver the library had never heard of, found a clock register the chip ships wrong, measured all of it, and documented every pin. It's on the flasher as a BETA, which means exactly what it always has here: it runs, nobody has watched a browser install of it yet, and if yours goes wrong we want the issue. The four-part esptool command is in `docs/NM-CYD-C5.md` if the browser won't play. Two things to know: it has no hardware for decimal maths, so it draws a little slower than the Xtensa boards (about 20 frames a second on most backgrounds), and it has no spare flash for the black box, so it keeps no crash history. It does run WiFi, Bluetooth, touch, the squad radio and the crypto self-test, and it's been drawing a wizard and a visiting Super Squach side by side all afternoon.

**The aquarium learned to count.** For that chip's sake the tank's maths was redone in whole numbers: the light shafts worked out once a frame instead of once a row, a little sine table instead of the real thing, and the fish read their shape from a table instead of computing it. On the C5 the tank went from 8 frames a second to 15. On every other board it looks the same and costs the same; a few hundred pixels a frame land a shade differently and nobody can find them.

**Yzzerd and OVER 9000 draw leaner.** Nothing under a robe or a gi gets painted any more, feet under slippers and boots are skipped, and the wizard's hat, slippers, moustache and shoulder pieces are outlined once instead of four times. Yzzerd paints a quarter fewer pixels a frame, OVER 9000 eight percent fewer, and on the 3.2" that's about two milliseconds back. On a real board Yzzerd and OVER 9000 cost the same, about 14 ms a frame with the aura on, against plain Squachy's 10.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- OVER 9000, a new outfit: tap his shades while the Legend's aura is lit. A scouter reads his power level, and the first time it passes nine thousand the outfit is his. Hints on any background while the aura is lit. The master unlock includes it.
- RockBase NM-CYD-C5 (ESP32-C5) support, `[env:nm-cyd-c5]`, by quietradio (#21). On the flasher as a BETA; the esptool route is in `docs/NM-CYD-C5.md`.
- Console: `OUTFIT n` wears costume n until the next boot and `AURA` toggles the aura, for timing things on a board. `LEGEND` stays.

**Changed**
- The squad radio's outfit field is five bits: seventeen outfits fit. Older boards show a visiting OVER 9000 as plain Squachy.
- The aquarium's per-row, per-column and per-fish maths runs in whole numbers.
- Yzzerd, OVER 9000, and four older outfits (space suit, both plumbers, the captain) no longer paint what their costume covers; Yzzerd's hat, slippers, moustache and shoulder pieces are outlined once.
- The outfit gallery in the README shows all sixteen costumes.
